research: Line: slate Auburn +2.5; archive open and close both +2.5. Predictem says the line opened with Auburn a small favorite and flipped to Arizona about -3; Covers says Arizona opened -1.5 (both Nov 13). The market moved toward Arizona early, then settled at the slate number - priced.
Total 159.5 at open and close (slate archive), though Predictem cites 157.5 -> 159.5.
Venue: a true road game at Neville Arena in Auburn (Predictem; Covers, Nov 13), not a neutral site.
[angle] Auburn has a 69-game non-conference home winning streak, the longest in the country, and no non-conference home loss in 10 years (Predictem; Covers, Nov 13) - Auburn.

[angle] Arizona already lost to UCLA 84-75 in its opener in Las Vegas despite Ivan Kharchenkov's 38 points, and fell from No. 5 to No. 12 (Predictem UCLA preview, Nov 11; Predictem, Nov 13) - mild Auburn.

Arizona shoots only about 28% from three and lives at the rim; 7-2 Motiejus Krivas shoots 73.1% (Predictem, Nov 13). Auburn blocks 8.5 shots a game and has held both opponents under 60 (Predictem, Nov 13). Rim scoring against rim protection - Auburn.
Auburn ranks 263rd in defensive rebounding rate (KenPom via Covers, Nov 13). Kharchenkov (24.7 points, 9 rebounds) and Krivas should win the glass - Arizona.

Tahaad Pettiford leads the SEC at 22.0 points and scored a career-high 30 in last December's 97-68 loss at Arizona; Auburn shoots about 40% from three and its bench scores about 35 a game (Predictem, Nov 13) - Auburn.
Under Tommy Lloyd, Arizona is 44-28-3 ATS in non-conference games and 37-17 in true road games (Covers; Predictem, Nov 13) - ATS records are priced, mild Arizona.
Auburn went 8-14 ATS as an underdog last season, and Covers expects regression after its first non-NCAA Tournament season since 2021 (Covers, Nov 13) - mild Arizona.
Projections: KenPom has Auburn by 2 (Covers, Nov 13); Predictem's tempo model has Arizona by about 3.5, 79-76 (Nov 13). The models split around the line - neutral.
Preview picks: Covers Arizona -2.5 (good to -4.5); Predictem has no side, only Under 159.5 (Nov 13) - priced.
games.reasoning: The models split (KenPom Auburn by 2, Torvik-style Arizona by 3.5) and the line sits between them at Arizona -2.5 after an early move toward Arizona. The most interesting angle is Auburn's shot-blocking against an Arizona offense that can't shoot threes, offset by Auburn's weak defensive rebounding against Arizona's size. Pass. Forced Arizona on the glass edge and the market move.

research: Line: slate Alabama -17.5; archive open -15.5, close -18.5. The market moved toward Alabama even with Davis-Fleming's doubtful status known, so the slate's -17.5 is a point better for Alabama than the close - priced.
Total 156.5 at open and close (slate archive).
KenPom projects Alabama by about 13, and Torvik's adjusted efficiency has Alabama by single digits (Predictem, Nov 13). Both are under the number - mild Seton Hall.
Alabama averages 102 points, ranks 5th in KenPom adjusted offense and plays one of the fastest tempos (Predictem, Nov 13) - Alabama.
Alabama beat Oakland 109-68, making 24 of 46 threes (one short of the school record); London Jemison went 6-of-6 from three (Predictem, Nov 13). Unsustainable shooting - mild Seton Hall.
[angle] Aden Holloway returned from suspension vs Oakland and made four threes (Predictem, Nov 13), so Alabama's backcourt is whole again for the first time this season - mild Alabama.

[angle] Jamarion Davis-Fleming, a 6-10 Mississippi State transfer and one of Alabama's best rebounders, missed the Oakland game with a lower-leg injury, hasn't practiced and is questionable; Nate Oats was 'not optimistic' (Predictem, Nov 13). The close moved toward Alabama anyway, so it is priced - mild Seton Hall.
Alabama ranks 297th in offensive rebound rate allowed (37.7%), and Oakland outrebounded it 37-31 (Predictem, Nov 13) - Seton Hall.

Seton Hall allows 54.7 points a game (top 15), has a top-25 adjusted defense per Barttorvik, holds opponents to a 22.1% offensive rebound rate (21st) and plays a slow tempo in the high 60s (Predictem, Nov 13) - Seton Hall.

[angle] Seton Hall's offense ranks outside the top 100 and it beat Charlotte only 68-62 on a neutral floor. A cold stretch could let Alabama's pace run away (Predictem, Nov 13), and LESSONS says a big underdog covers only if it can score - Alabama.
This is the first power-conference opponent for both teams (Predictem, Nov 13) - neutral.
Writer's pick Seton Hall +17.5, good to +14, projecting 84-72 (Predictem, Nov 13) - priced, tiebreaker only.
games.reasoning: KenPom (13) sits below the number, but the market moved three points toward Alabama to -18.5 with the Davis-Fleming news already out, and LESSONS says to treat the close as fair. Shading toward the close gives about 18, within 2 of the slate, so pass. The most interesting angle is Seton Hall's defense and rebounding against Alabama's weak defensive glass, offset by a Seton Hall offense that may not keep pace. Forced Alabama: the close moved its way.
